why_it_moved.text: Successful Search Rate rose 0.81% and Latency p95 rose 1.20% in the same test arm.
why_it_moved.label: measured

why_it_moved.text: A heavier ranking model plausibly costs extra serving time, which would explain the latency rise.
why_it_moved.label: inferred

why_it_moved.text: No segment cuts were in the scorecard, so why the success rate rose is not known.
why_it_moved.label: guess

would_change: A latency owner accepting the 1.20% rise, or a fix that brings it back near zero, would clear the guardrail concern.
A rerun with latency past the 2.00% margin would make the harm a breach.
A pre-exposure comparison and a daily series by days since first exposure would let the two checks that could not run be run.
